name: Caspian
description: Caspian, also presented as Caspco, describes its work as enterprise software development, application customization, and infrastructure implementation. Its corporate communications identify banking projects with Parsian Bank, although the evidence inspected does not establish a complete current core-banking product portfolio. [s1]

seo.title: Caspian: Banking Software and Enterprise Systems | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: An evidence-limited introduction to Caspian's enterprise software activities and its reported work with Parsian Bank.

content.heading: An enterprise software provider
content.content:
Caspian's corporate LinkedIn profile uses the name Caspco and describes a business spanning customized enterprise applications, adaptation of packaged software, and implementation of software and hardware infrastructure. This is a broader remit than a single banking application: the company presents itself as an enterprise technology supplier. [s1]

For this page, Caspian refers to that software business. The inspected profile provides the clearest available identification, but it is a company-authored account rather than an independently audited corporate history. [s1]

content.heading: Reported work with Parsian Bank
content.content:
A corporate update attributes the design, development, and implementation of Parsvam to Caspian. It describes Parsvam as a remote lending platform for Parsian Bank, including application processing, digital signatures, and a loan calculator. These are the supplier's descriptions of functionality; they do not independently establish customer uptake, credit outcomes, or service reliability. [s1]

The available evidence supports a focused introduction to Caspian's banking software activities. It does not yet support a detailed account of its core platform, deployment history, or competitive position.

name: Informatics Services Corporation
description: Informatics Services Corporation, commonly abbreviated ISC, works across Iranian banking technology and payment infrastructure. Inspected sources describe both a core-banking development programme and a wider role connected to the Central Bank of Iran and national payment networks. [s1] [s2]

seo.title: Informatics Services Corporation: Banking Infrastructure | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: ISC's documented banking technology role, core-banking announcements, and the limits of available operational evidence.

content.heading: Banking technology beyond a single platform
content.content: Informatics Services Corporation occupies a place in Iran's banking technology landscape that extends beyond supplying an individual bank application. In a dated account, the U.S. Treasury described ISC as a subsidiary and technology arm of the Central Bank of Iran. It identified ISC with oversight of Shetab, Iran's electronic banking clearance network, and an affiliation with Shaparak, the electronic card payment network. Treasury also attributed development of the central bank's digital currency platform to ISC. These descriptions are explicitly Treasury's account, rather than a verified current organization chart. [s1]

content.heading: A core-banking development announcement
content.content:
An announcement on the channel identifying itself as ISC's corporate channel described a new core-banking platform under development. The project manager said it was being designed around BIAN, the Banking Industry Architecture Network standard, and described its approach as modular. The announcement scheduled initial testing for Esfand 1400 in Iran's Solar Hijri calendar. Its wording concerns intended testing and development; it does not establish that the platform subsequently entered production. [s2]

A separate management statement on the same channel discussed core-banking processing alongside payment switching and national payment systems. This demonstrates the breadth of the company's own operational account, but the statement supplies neither a comparable annual dataset nor an independent availability assessment. Performance claims should therefore remain attributed to management. [s2]

content.heading: A dated international constraint
content.content:
On February 14, 2024, the U.S. Treasury announced ISC's designation under Executive Order 13224, as amended, for support to the Central Bank of Iran. Treasury also alleged involvement in a network procuring restricted U.S. technology. The announcement establishes the U.S. government's action and stated rationale; its allegations are not presented here as an independent judicial finding. [s1]

That dated action is relevant to understanding the organization's international technology context. This page does not establish the complete legal position at the editorial cutoff or assess any particular transaction.

name: Banking Systems Developers
description: Banking systems development includes building, maintaining, and supporting software for banking transactions and customer information. This page provisionally treats the supplied title as a professional activity because the research did not establish an Iranian organization with that exact English name. [s1]

seo.title: Banking Systems Developers: Scope and Evidence | Iran, Unfolded
seo.description: A provisional explanation of banking systems development while the identity intended by this taxonomy entry remains unresolved.

content.heading: What the work involves
content.content:
A primary example from outside Iran helps define the occupation without inventing a local company. Credo Bank's published core-banking development team-leader description covers design, implementation, maintenance, and enhancement of banking software. It connects development work with business requirements, code review, database extraction, incident investigation, and coordination across teams. [s1]

The example illustrates that banking systems development extends beyond writing a customer-facing application. It includes maintaining the routines and interfaces on which banking operations depend, and providing specialist support when problems arise. This is evidence of the role described by that employer, not proof of a uniform job structure or technology stack across Iranian banks. [s1]

content.heading: The Iranian subject remains unresolved
content.content: The supplied taxonomy places this title beside named banking software companies, but does not provide a Persian legal name or company URL. Research did not resolve whether it denotes an organization, a translated business name, or developers as a group. An Iran-specific company history, product catalogue, and contact listing therefore remain unwritten pending identification.
